Release note WorkSlop v16 · 23 October 2026 · by Adnan.120hz

Tweak iOS 16 to 27.0.1 without a jailbreak.

WorkSlop changes the parts of iOS that have no Settings page: icon packs, the status bar, Liquid Glass blur, animated wallpapers. WorkSlop Desktop v16 runs from your computer over USB; WorkSlop Mobile v3.0 runs on the phone itself. Every tweak on this page carries its test status — tested on my own phone, not confirmed yet, or doesn't work. Nothing here is padded out.

What it changes

If iOS Settings already does it, it isn't in here. WorkSlop only carries tweaks for things Apple gives you no switch for. Each one is marked with where it actually stands.

Custom icons — iOS 18 pack Tested · 26.6.1

51 apps in Light and Dark, drawn by catwithabaloon. Desktop puts them on the phone as WebClips, with the two modes side by side so each "add all" only touches its own table. I put this pack on my own phone on 26.6.1 and it stuck — after that I froze the menu. It stays exactly as tested.

Icon themes on Mobile New · Mobile v3.0

The iOS 18 pack, applied from the phone itself: Light, Dark and Tinted tables from the official catwithabaloon artwork, picked per app or all at once. The Icon Themes screen previews your own home screen before and after — those two shots in the Screens section are that preview, from a real phone.

Liquid Glass controls Tested on device

Blur and motion changes for the glass interface in iOS 26, all on the v4 code — including Blurr Motion and the animation-speed tweak, both running on my phone.

Status bar & fake 5G Label not confirmed

Rewrite the status bar, and set the network label to 5G, 5G+, 5G UW or 5G UC. It goes through the same statusBarOverrides file as my tested status-bar tweaks — but I still haven't seen the 5G label on a real screen, so it isn't marked tested.

Wallpapers & themes (PosterBoard) In the build

Animated wallpapers and lock-screen templates from .tendies files, plus .batter templates. The importer checks the file type before anything is written — a .tendies file only lands on the PosterBoard table, a .batter only on Templates.

Tweaks, daemons & MobileGestalt Checked before writing

SpringBoard options, daemon switches, MobileGestalt edits such as Dynamic Island toggles. HotLoad reads each payload before it goes to the phone and warns you about the risky ones first.

Sideload, app data & backup In the build

Install IPA files over USB, look inside app containers, and run the backup steps that iOS 26 and iOS 27 each ask for before any tweak can be applied at all.

How it gets onto your phone

No jailbreak means the tweaks have to arrive some other way. There are two apps and two routes, and which ones apply to you depends on your phone and your iOS.

From a computer — Desktop

WorkSlop Desktop runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Plug the phone in over USB, tap Trust, pick your tweaks, apply.

Two interfaces are included — the current WorkSlop UI and the older Nugget-style one — and you can switch between them.

On the phone — Mobile

WorkSlop Mobile does the same tweaks without the computer. You import a pairing file once; after that it talks to the phone over a loopback WireGuard tunnel.

v3.0 has a new interface: two menu sliders — Home, Liquid Glass, Recommend and SpringBoard across the top; Icon Themes, Apple Internal, Status Bar, Daemons and PosterBoard along the bottom — over an animated background of drifting Apple logos. The glass effect is always on.

iOS 26 vs iOS 27

On iOS 26 the tweaks go in through the partial-restore route. On iOS 27 they use the protective full-backup route: backup first, then apply, then restore.

The app picks the route for your iOS — you just need to know they're different before you start.

Managed profiles

Two configuration profiles you can install straight from this page — no computer, no app needed. They install side by side and don't overwrite each other. iOS always asks you first; nothing here installs silently.

FeatureFlags profile Experimental · untested

A .mobileconfig carrying a "com.apple.system.featureflags" payload. The payload key names (Features, Domain, FeatureName, Enabled) are real strings from the iOS 26.6.1 firmware; the feature entry inside is our best research guess and is untested. The "isAllowedToWriteFeatureFlags" gate is intact on iOS 26.6.1, so an ordinary iPhone will most likely reject this profile at install. A rejection is the expected outcome there — it means the gate did its job, not that the file is broken.

Download workslop-featureflags.mobileconfig ↓

WorkSlop home-screen bookmark Installs normally

A normal WebClip profile. Install it and a WorkSlop icon appears on your home screen — tap it to open this website. It changes no system setting, and you can delete it like any app icon.

Download workslop-webclip-bookmark.mobileconfig ↓

How to install either one: tap the download link above — the file goes straight to your iPhone. Then open Settings → Profile Downloaded → Install and confirm the prompts. Your iPhone will ask for your approval before installing the profile — nothing installs silently. If you installed the FeatureFlags one, reboot afterwards — flags are read at launch, so a reboot is the only way to judge any effect.

Latest iOS 27 info

What WorkSlop currently does — and doesn't do — on iOS 27. Updated 23 October 2026; this is the newest information on this page.

Supported iOS 27 versions G1 engine

The iOS 27 apply route only runs on: iOS 27.0 Developer Beta 1–9, iOS 27.0 RC, iOS 27.0 stable, and iOS 27.0.1. Anything else is refused with "Not supported" before anything is written to the phone.

How the iOS 27 method works 100% new

Full backup of all the phone's data to the computer → a payload is built from whichever tweaks you enabled (dozens of locations, matched to your active tweaks) → the payload is injected into the backup and verified byte-for-byte → the phone is restored from the modified backup via a dedicated restore function written from scratch for iOS 27 → reboot with notification. No sparse-restore phase, no selective wipe, no leftover code from the old method. A stall watchdog stops the process safely if the device goes quiet. A risk warning has to be confirmed first.

Honest labels Read this

The G1 pipeline ran start to finish on two real devices on iOS 26.6.1 RC — user data stayed intact, and the result comes back to the cable you use and how stable the iPhone–laptop connection is. It has not been tested on a real iPhone running iOS 27 yet. The FeatureFlags managed profile above is untested on retail iPhones — the install gate is intact on iOS 26.6.1, so expect it to be rejected there.

Why the current builds do iOS 27 this way v15 → v16

On iOS 27, the current route is much safer than v14's: it takes a full backup of all your data first, builds a payload from the tweaks you enabled, modifies it, then restores the phone from the modified backup. The trade-off: it takes much longer than the quick partial-restore route iOS 26 uses. This is not a partial restore — the two iOS versions take different routes. The method worked on two real devices on iOS 26.6.1 RC; it has not been tested on a real iPhone on iOS 27 yet.

WorkSlop Mobile on iOS 27 Partially supported

Mobile's iOS 27 route runs on the phone itself, and the beta team is testing it now — it is not finished. Two things matter before you apply: Find My must be off, and keep at least 14 GB of storage free — the protective backup is written on the phone itself, and a nearly-full phone runs out of room mid-apply. On iOS 26 the route is tested and none of this applies.

iOS 27 — do not use Desktop v14

iOS 27 · can bootloop

Warning: WorkSlop Desktop v14 must not be used on iOS 27 — it can put the iPhone into a bootloop. One iPhone on iOS 27 bootlooped on v14 and was recovered via an IPSW restore from backup. Use the newest build on this page instead.

Tutorial from scratch

Never used WorkSlop before? Start here. Two ways to run it: from your computer (WorkSlop Desktop) or on the phone itself (WorkSlop Mobile). Pick one — you don't need both.

On the computer — WorkSlop Desktop

01
Download WorkSlop for your OS

Windows gets the v16 beta; macOS and Linux are on v15 — both are in the Download section below. Unzip it and run the app.

02
Plug in your iPhone with a good cable

Use a proper cable — not a worn-out one. Tap Trust on the phone and enter your passcode. On Windows, if the phone doesn't show up, install Apple Devices from the Microsoft Store first.

03
Back up the phone

Make a full backup before you touch anything. If a tweak goes wrong, this backup is what saves you.

04
Turn Find My off

Off before every Apply; turn it back on when you're done.

05
Pick tweaks, press Apply

Start with one tweak, not ten. On iOS 26 the app uses the quick partial-restore route. On iOS 27 it uses the full backup → payload → restore route — much safer, but much longer. Don't unplug anything while it runs.

06
Reboot by hand, check, repeat

Restart the phone yourself after applying, verify the tweak took, then try the next one. One at a time.

On the phone — WorkSlop Mobile

01
Install the app

WorkSlop Mobile is an unsigned IPA — sideload it onto your iPhone with your usual signing method.

02
Pair it with your phone

Open the app and follow the on-screen pairing steps until the device card shows your phone as connected.

03
Back up first, then apply

Same rules as desktop: back up the phone, turn Find My off, apply one tweak at a time, reboot by hand, and check the result before moving on.

Three things that break phones: a bad cable, unplugging mid-apply, and skipping the backup. WorkSlop is most useful on iOS 26. The owner (Adnan.120hz) is not responsible for any damage — use your phone at your own risk.

Before you press Apply

WorkSlop writes to places iOS doesn't officially open up. Five things to do first — every time, not just the first time.

01
Back up the phone first

A full backup before you apply or reset anything. If a tweak goes wrong, this is what you come back to.

02
Turn Find My off — it must be off

Find My iPhone must be turned off before every Apply and every Reset, on Desktop and Mobile alike. Back on afterwards.

03
USB in, tap Trust, stay plugged in

On Windows, if the phone doesn't show up, install Apple Devices first.

04
Know which route your iOS takes

iOS 26 goes through partial restore; iOS 27 through the protective full-backup route. Not the same steps.

05
Restart by hand, then test one tweak at a time

Restart after applying, and change one thing before you test the next.

One hard rule on iOS 26.6.1: never reset the SpringBoard home-screen pages from the app — it can break the home screen at boot. Resetting the Liquid Glass pages is fine.
